# pillar-csi

> pillar-csi is a Kubernetes CSI driver written in Go. It creates ZFS zvols and LVM logical volumes on your storage nodes and exports them to pods over NVMe-oF/TCP through the Linux kernel nvmet target. It is licensed under Apache-2.0.

pillar-csi has three components. pillar-agent runs as a DaemonSet on storage nodes, manages zvols and logical volumes, and writes the kernel nvmet configfs tree directly, reading each write back. pillar-controller runs as a Deployment and reconciles the cluster-scoped CRDs PillarAgent, PillarStore, PillarProtocol, and PillarStorageClass. pillar-node runs as a DaemonSet on worker nodes, connects to the target, formats the device with ext4 or xfs, and mounts it.

Supported backends are ZFS zvols and LVM logical volumes. The only supported protocol is NVMe-oF/TCP; iSCSI, NFS, and SMB are not supported yet. Access modes are ReadWriteOnce, ReadWriteOncePod, and ReadOnlyMany; ReadWriteMany is rejected. pillar-csi does not replicate data, so a volume is unavailable while its storage node is down. The host must provide the nvme_tcp and nvme_fabrics kernel modules on worker nodes and nvmet and nvmet_tcp on storage nodes. The Helm chart is published at oci://ghcr.io/isac322/charts/pillar-csi, and `agent.backends` in values.yaml is empty by default, so an install must configure at least one backend. mTLS for the controller-to-agent gRPC channel is optional and off by default.

- [First PVC tutorial](https://pillar-csi.bhyoo.com/docs/tutorials/first-pvc/): from a storage node with a ZFS pool or LVM volume group to a pod with a mounted volume
